messages.subject_clean: The MPlus error message prior to "MODEL FIT INFORMATION"
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Thanks for providing another example of warnings/errors that need to be registered by readModels. A fellow Github user (patr1ckm) was kind enough to provide initial code to read estimation errors and warnings. I adapted and extended this code and just merged it all into the development version of the package. This is a particularly tricky section to parse because of its irregular format and position in the output file, so please forward me output files where the warnings and errors are not handled appropriately. I will try to roll this and other changes out to CRAN soon for general use.

require(devtools)

install_github("MplusAutomation", "michaelhallquist")

Best,
Michael

messages.subject: Re: Error in readModel when reading a latent class model
messages.subject_clean: Error in readModel when reading a latent class model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Annibale,

Thanks for forwarding the problematic output file. It turns out that this file contains a new section header "Available post-processing tools:" that I had never seen before (probably new in v7.2?), which was throwing off the section parser. I have added this header to the list and your file now parses correctly. Incidentally, your residuals output also had section headers named "Model Estimated Means" instead of the typical "Model Estimated Means/Intercepts/Thresholds", so your residuals were also not being parsed. I added the new section naming to the residuals parser, too. Both of these problems underscore how fragile the text parsing approach can be for reading Mplus output files... If one section header changes or is added, there's no way to catch it until a problematic output file is identified. Anyhow, these problems are fixed in the development version on Github. I'm planning to roll out recent changes to CRAN soon, too.

Best,
Michael

messages.subject: Re: Error message?
messages.body_plain:
I suspect there is a problem with your X11 installation, or perhaps a collision between installed versions of Tcl/Tk. This is not really an MplusAutomation issue, but an issue with your setup of Tcl/Tk. Given the "image not found" error for libX11.6.dylib, if it were me, I would reinstall X11. If you have additional problems, you might post your question to stackoverflow or to R help, as those folks might have more experience with Tcl/Tk problems.

Best,
Michael

But when I try to run these commands (which are the ones I really need to function):

mplus.get.estimated_means
mplus.plot.estimated_means

I keep getting this error:

Error in gh5$means_and_variances_data$y_estimated_means$values[i, var_indices[j]] : subscript out of bounds

What should I do?

Thanks much.
